newsitem.title: UK: Hong Kong monetary autonomy will stay - Hkg official.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong monetary autonomy will stay - Hkg official.

text.p: Hong Kong will have even more monetary autonomy once it comes under Chinese rule next year, head of the Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) Joseph Yam said on Tuesday.

"Notwithstanding the high degree of monetary authority Hong Kong has been enjoying, there will in fact be an even higher degree of monetary autonomy...as a result of the transfer of sovereignty," Yam said in a speech prepared for delivery at a Bank of England seminar.
The HKMA has the framework to robustly defend that autonomy, he added.
Yam described as myths speculation that once China took over there would be massive capital flight, that the Hong Kong dollar would disappear or the exchange rate link would be abandoned.
The Joint Declaration and Basic Law covering Hong Kong and the change of sovereignty also contained clear safeguards against its substantial reserves being absorbed by China, he said.
"The playing field will not be tilted in favour of Mainland interests after 1997," Lam said, adding Hong Kong would maintain its regulatory standards.
"We are highly conscious of our supervisory and other central banking responsibilities and have the means to ensure that they are carried out in an honest and impartial manner after 1997," he said.
